summary: @servicetitan/web-components 38.1.7 preinstall dropper executes obfuscated payload via smuggled Bun runtime
details: Version 38.1.7 of @servicetitan/web-components ships a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun (bun-v1.3.13 release), extracts it, chmods it executable, and uses `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727 KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob featuring a `@bun @bun-cjs` header, a rotating string-array (`WV8StW`), and a custom-alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`). Neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` is listed in the package.json `files` manifest (`["dist","src"]`), and the preinstall script itself is a newly added entry not present in the package's normal build. The Bun runtime is fetched specifically to execute the payload outside Node, evading Node-based require-graph inspection. The package's stated purpose is a microfrontend web-components framework, which has no legitimate need for an out-of-manifest 727 KB obfuscated file executed under an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time. `npm install` of this version yields arbitrary code execution on the installer's host via attacker-controlled payload content.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
